headers.description: Optional headers to send with the request as a dictionary of header values.

Authorization.description: The credentials to authenticate a user agent with a server, typically formatted as 'Bearer {token}'.

timeout.description: The maximum amount of time to wait for a response from the server, in seconds. A longer timeout may be necessary for slower network connections or overloaded servers. This is a float type value.

params.description: URL parameters to append to the URL. Sent as a dictionary of key-value pairs.

query.description: The query parameter for search or filtering.

page.description: The page number parameter for pagination. Used to retrieve a specific page of results.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials formatted as a tuple of strings (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem), if required for the request.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names and values.

sessionid.description: Session identifier cookie, used to recognize client sessions on the server.

csrftoken.description: CSRF protection token cookie, used to prevent cross-site request forgery attacks.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary, mapping protocol or protocol and hostname to the URL of the proxy.

http.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTP requests, including the port number.

https.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTPS requests, including the port number.

stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not. Set to False to skip certificate verification, which is not recommended unless you are sure of the server's identity.

message.content:
Here’s how you can quickly zero‑in on a quick flick right around Times Square—no more than two hours and definitely walkable!

| Theater | Address | Nearby Landmark | Example Film (≤ 120 min) |
|---------|--------|-----------------|--------------------------|
| **AMC Empire 25** | 234 W 42nd St, New York, NY 10036 | Just steps from Times Square & Bryant Park | *“Cinderella”* (Runtime ≈ 90 min) |
| **Regal Cinema Times Square** | 225 W 41st St, New York, NY 10123 | Across the street from Broadway theatres | *“Encanto”* (Runtime ≈ 76 min) |
| **Alamo Drafthouse Cinema** | 200 W 34th St, New York, NY 10001 | Near Penn Station & Grand Central | *“The Princess Bride”* (Runtime ≈ 97 min) |

### Quick Steps to Book

1. **Pick a theater**  
   All three locations sit inside the Midtown Manhattan block bounded by 40–43rd Streets and 8th–9th Avenue—well within a five‑minute stroll from Times Square itself.

2. **Check the official site / app**  
   • AMC: `https://www.amctheatres.com/movie-theaters/amc-empires-25`  
   • Regal: `https://reglacinema.com/theater/regal-cinema-times-square`  
   • Alamo: `http://drafthouse.com/new-york`

   These sites let you filter by “Showtime” → “Today” and see runtimes directly.

3. **Confirm runtime ≤ 120 minutes**  
   Most listings display the exact length next to each title. Look for titles marked “Short,” “Family,” or “Animated”—they’re usually under 90 minutes.

4. **Reserve seats**  
   Once you’ve chosen a film, book through the same portal or via popular ticket platforms (Fandango, Atom Tickets).

---

#### Why this works

- **Walking Distance:** Each venue lies less than 400 m (~½ mile) from Times Square, meaning you’ll spend virtually all your travel time strolling rather than commuting.
- **Duration Filtered:** By selecting only those films flagged as “short” or “family-friendly,” you automatically stay below the 2‑hour mark.
- **Real-Time Availability:** Checking the theater’s own booking system guarantees up-to-date seat availability and avoids last‑minute surprises.

Enjoy your cinema adventure—and feel free to ask me anything else about getting there!
